hindi: अब इसके बाद हम रोगानुत्पादनीय नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the non-arising of diseases (Rogānutpādanīya).

words.gloss: wind, stool, urine, sneeze, thirst, hunger
sleep, cough, exertion, breath, yawning, tears, vomiting, semen

hindi: वात, मल, मूत्र, छींक, प्यास और भूख के वेगों को न रोके; तथा नींद, खाँसी, श्रम से चढ़ी साँस, जम्भाई, आँसू, वमन और वीर्य के वेगों को भी न रोके।
english: One should not hold back the urges of wind (flatus), stool, urine, sneezing, thirst and hunger, nor those of sleep, cough, laboured breathing from exertion, yawning, tears, vomiting and semen.
notes: Genitive plural compounds depend on vegān (urges). śrama-śvāsa is taken as two members, 'exertion' and 'breath'; the book's split also separates them, and it may be read 'breathing from exertion'. Printed 'ccharddi' is a spelling variant of chardi.

words.gloss: retention of wind, urine and stool, damage to sight and agni, heart ailments
words.gram: mixed compound (dvandva of tat-puruṣas), m. nom. pl.

hindi: नीचे जाने वाली वायु के रोकने से गुल्म, उदावर्त, पीड़ा और थकान होती है; वायु, मूत्र और मल का रुक जाना, दृष्टि और अग्नि की हानि तथा हृदय के रोग भी होते हैं।
english: From suppressing the downward wind there arise gulma, udāvarta, pain and fatigue, retention of wind, urine and stool, impairment of sight and of the digestive fire (agni), and ailments of the heart.
notes: gulma and udāvarta are kept as named conditions. 'vadha' is taken as damage or loss, applying to both sight and agni; saṅga could also apply only to the three listed items. The verb ('arise') is understood.

words.gloss: making the wind move in its proper course

hindi: इस दशा में स्नेहन और स्वेदन की विधि, बत्तियाँ, भोजन, पेय और बस्तियाँ हितकर कही गई हैं, जो वायु को अपने ठीक मार्ग पर चलाने वाली हैं।
english: In this case the procedure of oleation and sweating, wicks, foods, drinks and also enemas are recommended, as what sets the wind moving in its proper course.
notes: śastam (singular) with the plural list is collective. vātānulomanam is read as qualifying the whole list ('that which makes the wind move along its proper course'); it could also be read as a further item.

hindi: मल के रोकने से पिंडलियों में ऐंठन, प्रतिश्याय और सिर की पीड़ा होती है; वायु ऊपर की ओर चढ़ती है, काटने जैसी पीड़ा होती है और हृदय में रुकावट होती है।
english: From (suppressing) stool: twisting cramps of the calves, nasal catarrh and head pain; wind moving upward, cutting pain, and obstruction of the heart.
notes: śakṛtaḥ is genitive, depending on the understood 'rodhāt/rodhena' (suppression). 'parikartaḥ' is masculine here (usually parikartikā). ūrdhvaṃ vāyuḥ could also be 'upward wind (as a condition)'.

words.gloss: body-ache, stone, pains of bladder, penis and groin
words.gram: mixed compound (dvandva with tat-puruṣa), f. nom. pl.

hindi: मुख से मल का निकलना और पहले कहे हुए रोग भी बताए गए हैं; अंगों का टूटना, पथरी, तथा मूत्राशय, लिंग और जाँघ के जोड़ में पीड़ा।
english: Passing of stool through the mouth, and the ailments stated before, are recorded; breaking pain in the limbs, stone, and pains in the bladder, penis and groin.
notes: GROUPING: the second line (5.11) begins the list of ailments of suppressed urine and its verb is syuḥ mūtrarodhāt in the first line of the next unit (7); the first line belongs with the preceding stool topic. Right grouping: 5.10 as a one-line unit closing the stool topic, then 5.11 + 5.12 forming one verse (5.12 also runs on into the remedy list of 5.13). The printed two-line pairing is kept here. aśmarī is rendered 'stone' (literal).

hindi: मूत्र के रोकने से (ये रोग) हो सकते हैं, और पहले कहे हुए रोग भी प्रायः होते हैं; उनकी औषधि है बत्तियाँ, अभ्यंग, अवगाहन, स्वेदन और बस्तिकर्म।
english: From suppression of urine (the ailments just listed) may arise, and mostly the earlier diseases too; their remedy is wicks, anointing, immersion baths, sweating and enema treatment.

text_flags.why: possible: lacks the r of vartti (unit 4 has 'varttayaḥ') and has an extra anusvāra after a (aṃbhyaṃ- for abhyaṅ-); the book's split has वर्ति

notes: GROUPING: this unit's first line completes the verse begun in the second line of unit 6 (5.11 + 5.12). 'pūrve' is read as the previously mentioned diseases; tadauṣadham 'its remedy' refers to the urine-suppression ailments. 'bastikarmaca' is printed without a space.

hindi: मल के रुकने से उत्पन्न क्षय-रोगों में मल को ढीला करने वाले अन्न और पेय देने चाहिए; और मूत्र से उत्पन्न रोगों में, तथा पान के विषय में, भोजन से पहले घी देना उचित कहा गया है।
english: In the wasting ailments (yakṣman) arising from retention of stool, food and drink that loosen the stool are to be used; and in those arising from urine, and in drinking, ghee before the meal is recommended.
notes: The first line has no finite verb; 'is recommended' is understood from the next line. 'pāne ca' is ambiguous (in drinking, i.e. ghee taken as a drink, or as the mode of intake); rendered literally. yakṣman is kept as the named group of wasting ailments, no modern diagnosis intended.
lines_deva: मूत्रजेषु तु पाने च प्राग्भक्ताच्छस्यते घृतं ॥
lines_iast: mūtrajeṣu tu pāne ca prāgbhaktācchasyate ghṛtaṃ ||

hindi: पाचन के अंत के समीप, सबसे बड़ी मात्रा से दो प्रकार का प्रयोग; यह अवपीडक नाम से कहा गया है। फिर रोकने से (आगे के रोग)।
english: Also (a use) near the end of digestion, with the highest dose, a twofold application; this is named avapīḍaka. Again, from holding back (the following ...).
notes: GROUPING: 'dhāraṇāt punaḥ' (5.17, flagged by the editors as a lead-in) opens the next sentence, 'dhāraṇāt punaḥ udgārasya aruciḥ kampaḥ ...' in unit 10; right grouping: unit 9 ends at 'saṃjñitam'. The first line is obscure: jīrṇāntikam and yojanādvayam may be read as 'ghee administered at the end of digestion in the highest dose, in two ways', or yojanā-dvayam as 'a pair of procedures'; the technical term avapīḍaka is kept untranslated. Translation is tentative.

uncertain.note: [hindi] "फिर वेगों को रोकने से" is a lead-in for the next topic, loosely attached — suggested: none

hindi: डकार को रोकने से भोजन में अरुचि, कंपन, हृदय और छाती में रुकावट, अफारा, खाँसी और हिचकी होती है; उसमें उपचार हिचकी के समान है।
english: From holding back a belch: distaste for food, tremor, obstruction in the heart and chest, distension, cough and hiccups; the remedy there is as for hiccups.
notes: 'From holding back' is taken from dhāraṇāt in the preceding line (5.17), see GROUPING in unit 9. hṛdayorasoḥ is a dual, read as locative.

words.gloss: weakness of senses, stiffness of neck, ardita
sharp smoke, collyrium, sniffing, nasal drops, the sun

hindi: छींक रोकने से सिर में पीड़ा, इंद्रियों की दुर्बलता, गर्दन की जकड़न और अर्दित होता है; तीखे धुएँ, अंजन, सूँघने, नस्य और सूर्य को देखने के द्वारा ... (क्रिया अगली इकाई में है)।
english: From suppressing a sneeze: head pain, weakness of the senses, stiffness of the neck and ardita; by sharp smoke, collyrium, sniffing, nasal drops and looking at the sun ... (the verb comes in the next unit).
notes: The sentence is completed in unit 12 (pravartayet kṣutim saktām). Printed 'śirortī' is śiraḥ + arti (normally śiro'rti). 'arka' is read as the sun, in 'looking at the sun'; it could also be a drug name, not decided. ardita is kept as a named ailment, no diagnosis given. kṣuteḥ is genitive/ablative of kṣuti.

hindi: रुकी हुई छींक को प्रवृत्त करे; स्वेदन और अभ्यंग का सेवन करे; वात को नष्ट करने वाला अन्न प्रयोग करे और भोजन के बाद घी दे।
english: One should bring on the held-back sneeze and practise sweating and anointing; wind-relieving food should be applied, and ghee after the meal.
notes: Printed 'pravarttayet' has a doubled t (spelling variant). uttarabhaktaka is read as 'after-meal (ghee)'.

words.gloss: dryness, limb-weariness, deafness, bewilderment, giddiness, heart ailments

hindi: प्यास को रोकने से शोष, अंगों की शिथिलता, बहरापन, मोह, चक्कर और हृदय के रोग होते हैं; उसमें हर शीतल उपाय हितकर है।
english: From restraining thirst: dryness (śoṣa), limb-weariness, deafness, bewilderment, giddiness and heart ailments; in that case every cooling procedure is beneficial.

words.gloss: body-ache, distaste for food, exhaustion, emaciation, colic pain, giddiness

hindi: भूख को रोकने से अंगों का टूटना, अरुचि, ग्लानि, दुबलापन, शूल और चक्कर होते हैं; उसमें हल्का, चिकना, गर्म और थोड़ा भोजन देना चाहिए।
english: From restraining hunger: breaking pain in the limbs, distaste for food, exhaustion, emaciation, colic pain and giddiness; in that case a light, unctuous, warm and small meal is to be given.
notes: kṣudhaḥ is genitive/ablative singular; 'from restraining' is understood from the pattern of the preceding units.

words.gloss: bewilderment, fainting, heavy eyes, laziness, yawning

hindi: नींद को रोकने से मोह, मूर्च्छा, आँखों में भारीपन, आलस्य, जम्भाई और अंगों में पीड़ा होती है; उसमें नींद और अंग दबाना (मालिश) इष्ट है।
english: From suppressing sleep: bewilderment, fainting, heaviness of the eyes, laziness, yawning, and aching of the limbs; in that case sleep and massage are desirable.
notes: 'iṣṭaḥ' agrees with svapnaḥ (saṃvāhanāni is added by ca). The printed line runs 'aṅgamardaścatatreṣṭaḥ' together; no change of letters needed.

words.gloss: breathlessness, distaste for food, heart ailments

hindi: खाँसी को रोकने से वही बढ़ती है, और साँस की कठिनाई, अरुचि और हृदय के रोग होते हैं; शोष और हिचकी भी होती है। यहाँ खाँसी को दूर करने वाली विधि विशेष रूप से करनी चाहिए।
english: From suppressing a cough: its increase, breathlessness, distaste for food and heart ailments, wasting (śoṣa) and hiccup; here the cough-relieving procedure is to be carried out all the more.
notes: 'śoṣo hidhmā ca' is read as two further effects (wasting, hiccup). The construction of kāryaḥ with vidhiḥ is as in the book's split.
lines_deva: शोषो हिध्मा च कार्योऽत्र कासहा सुतरां विधिः ॥
lines_iast: śoṣo hidhmā ca kāryo'tra kāsahā sutarāṃ vidhiḥ ||

words.gram: ppp. caus. vi-√dhṛ, m. abl. sg.

hindi: श्रम से उत्पन्न श्वास के रोकने पर गुल्म, हृदय का रोग और मोह होते हैं; उसमें विश्राम और वात को नष्ट करने वाला उपचार-क्रम हितकर है।
english: From holding back the laboured breathing of exertion: gulma, heart disease and bewilderment; in that case rest is beneficial, and a course of treatment that relieves wind.
notes: śrama-śvāsa read as 'breathing due to exertion'.

words.gloss: nasal affliction, pain in eyes, head, heart, stiff neck, distaste for food, giddiness

hindi: जम्भाई रोकने से छींक के समान रोग होते हैं, और वात को जीतने वाली हर विधि। पीनस, आँखों, सिर और हृदय में पीड़ा, गर्दन की जकड़न, अरुचि, चक्कर ... (वाक्य अगली इकाई में चलता है)।
english: From (holding back) a yawn: ailments like those of sneezing, and every procedure that overcomes wind. Nasal affliction (pīnasa), pain in the eyes, head and heart, stiff neck, distaste for food, giddiness ... (the sentence continues in the next unit).
notes: GROUPING: the second line (5.35) is the list of effects of suppressed tears and completes with 'bāṣpataḥ' in 5.36 (unit 19), so lines 5.35 + 5.36 form one verse; unit 18 should end at 5.34. The printed two-line pairing is kept; line 5.35 is translated here as the beginning of that list (effects of suppressed tears), completed in unit 19. 'Like those of sneezing' refers back to units 11-12.

words.gloss: visarpa, koṭha, skin disease (kuṣṭha), itching of eyes, pallor ailment, fevers

hindi: ... गुल्म सहित, आँसू रोकने से; उसमें नींद, मद्य और प्रिय कथाएँ। विसर्प, कोठ, कुष्ठ, आँखों की खुजली, पांडु रोग और ज्वर ... (वाक्य अगली इकाई में चलता है)।
english: ... together with gulma, from (holding back) tears; in that case sleep, liquor, pleasing talk. Visarpa, koṭha, skin disease (kuṣṭha), itching of the eyes, a pallor ailment (pāṇḍu-āmaya) and fevers ... (the sentence continues in the next unit).
notes: GROUPING: line 5.36 completes the verse started at 5.35 (unit 18). Line 5.37 begins the list of ailments of suppressed vomiting and is completed by 'sakāsa... vameḥ' in 5.38 (unit 20), so 5.37 + 5.38 form one verse. madyam is any intoxicating drink ('liquor'). visarpa, koṭha and pāṇḍu-āmaya are kept as named conditions.
lines_deva: सगुल्मा बाष्पतस्तत्र स्वप्नो मद्यं प्रियाः कथाः ॥
lines_iast: sagulmā bāṣpatastatra svapno madyaṃ priyāḥ kathāḥ ||

words.gloss: with cough, breathlessness, nausea, blemish, swellings
gargle, smoke, (upavāsa "fasting" conjectural; printed text corrupt), food

hindi: ... खाँसी सहित श्वास, मिचली, व्यंग और सूजन, वमन रोकने से; गण्डूष, धूम और आहार (छपा पाठ भ्रष्ट है; बीच का शब्द अनिश्चित); रूखा (भोजन) खाकर उसकी उलटी करना।
english: ... with cough, breathlessness, nausea, blemishes (vyaṅga) and swellings, from holding back vomiting; gargle, smoke, ... and food (the printed text is corrupt; a word between is uncertain); having eaten dry (food), vomiting it up.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed 'dhūmāvā-hāraṃ' does not yield a sensible compound; the editors' split reads dhūma-upavāsa-āhāram, but that makes the line longer than 16 syllables, so the text may be corrupt in another way

notes: GROUPING: 5.37 (unit 19 line 2) belongs with this unit's first line. The second line is damaged (editors' note on 5.39): the reading and the syntax of the list are uncertain and the translation is tentative. 'sa-' may apply to the whole list rather than to kāsa only. vyaṅga is rendered 'blemish' (a mark, esp. on the face). The printed two-line pairing is kept; the first line completes the list begun in unit 19.

uncertain.note: [src/split] `धूमावाहारं` does not yield `धूम उपवास आहारम्`; an upavāsa element is missing/garbled in src — suggested: `गंडूषधूमोपवासाहारं` or `गण्डूषधूमोपवासाः रूक्षं`

hindi: यहाँ व्यायाम, रक्त का निकालना और विरेचन उचित है; और अभ्यंग के लिए क्षार और नमक सहित तेल उचित कहा गया है।
english: Here exercise, the letting of blood and purgation are recommended; and oil with alkali and salt is recommended for anointing.

text_flags.why: possible: 'śruti' (hearing) makes no sense with asrasya; 'sruti' (flow, of blood) is the likely reading

notes: The printed token is 'śrutiḥ' in the Devanagari-derived text; the corrected word in the split is srutiḥ. 'srutir asrasya' is read as 'flow of blood', i.e. bloodletting. 'Alkali' for kṣāra is literal.

words.gloss: pain of the private part, swelling, fevers
heart pain, urine retention, limb-ache, enlargement, stone, impotence

hindi: वीर्य का बहना (पाठ अनिश्चित), गुप्तांग में पीड़ा, सूजन और ज्वर; हृदय में पीड़ा, मूत्र का रुकना, अंगों का टूटना, वृद्धि, पथरी और नपुंसकता।
english: Discharge of semen (reading of the first word uncertain), pain in the private part, swelling and fevers; heart pain, retention of urine, aching limbs, enlargement (vṛddhi), stone and impotence.

text_flags.why: possible: printed word is garbled (editors' note on 5.42); 'discharge of semen' fits the topic (retas, unit 2) and the book's Hindi; the syllable count then falls to 15, so another reading is not excluded
the printed 'hṛdyathā' lacks the v of hṛd-vyathā (heart pain); the book's split reads हृद् व्यथा

notes: The cause (suppression of semen, retas) is not stated in the unit; the list continues the pattern. The first word is damaged (editors' flag), so the translation of it is tentative. vṛddhi is rendered literally as 'enlargement' (commentators may specify a site).

uncertain.note: [src/split/eng] `शुकान्त्रत्रवणं` garbled; split `शुक आन्त्र श्रवणम्` is nonsense; Hindi says semen discharge — suggested: `शुक्रस्रवणं` (शुक्र स्रवणम्, discharge of semen); Eng "semen passage" to be revised accordingly

words.gloss: cock (tāmracūḍa), liquor, rice (śāli), enema, anointing, immersion bath

hindi: ताम्रचूड, सुरा, शालि, बस्ति, अभ्यंग और अवगाहन; तथा बस्ति की शुद्धि करने वाले द्रव्यों से सिद्ध किए हुए दूध का सेवन करे और प्रिय स्त्रियों का साथ करे।
english: Tāmracūḍa, surā, śāli rice, enema, anointing and immersion bath; and one should take milk prepared with (substances) that cleanse the bladder, and resort to beloved women.
notes: tāmracūḍa ('copper-crested', literally a cock) is kept as the name; whether it is food is not stated in the Sanskrit. 'basti' means both bladder and enema: in the compound it is an enema, in bastiśuddhikara it is read as the bladder; alternative 'enema-cleansing'. The unit's verb for the first line is understood (such things are to be used/practised).

words.gloss: by forcing out and holding back the urges

hindi: प्यास और शूल से पीड़ित, क्षीण, मल की उलटी करने वाले तथा वेगों को रोकने वाले रोगी को छोड़ देना चाहिए। सभी रोग वेगों को बलपूर्वक निकालने और रोकने से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: One should give up the patient who is afflicted by thirst and colic, wasted, vomiting stool, and a suppressor of urges. All diseases arise from forcing out and from holding back the urges.
notes: 'tyajet' (give up, i.e. not treat) is rendered literally. The first line may be read as one patient with all four marks, or as four separate descriptions; the single-patient reading is taken. 'vega' applies to both udīraṇa and dhāraṇa.

hindi: वहाँ मुख्य रूप से उपचार निर्दिष्ट किया गया है, परंतु उनके प्रति जो — (वाक्य यहाँ अधूरा है); और उनसे, इसलिए, अनेक प्रकार से प्रायः वायु प्रकुपित होती है।
english: There the remedy has been specified, chiefly, but with regard to those which (the clause is left incomplete here); and from these, therefore, in many ways, the wind (vāta) is generally provoked.
notes: The antecedent of 'ye ... tān' is not in this unit (it refers to disorders or causes named earlier), so the first line is rendered closely. 'yat' may be 'that/because'; the sentence continues in unit 26 where 'tasya' refers back to pavana. The editors' 'urges/suppression' in the book English is not in the Sanskrit.
lines_deva: निर्दिष्टं साधनं तत्र भूयिष्ठं ये तु तान्प्रति ॥
lines_iast: nirdiṣṭaṃ sādhanaṃ tatra bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ye tu tānprati ||

hindi: उसके लिए पीड़ित व्यक्ति अनुलोमन करने वाले अन्न, पान और औषध का प्रयोग करे, और उन-उन विकारों में प्रत्येक के अनुरूप चिकित्सा भी करे।
english: For it, the afflicted person should use food, drink and medicine that set it in its natural course (anulomana); and, in each of those disorders, the treatment suited to each.
notes: 'tasya' is taken as the wind (pavana) of unit 25; it could also be 'for him'. 'anulomana' is rendered literally ('with the grain'); the book's 'downward movement of vāta' is an interpretation. 'teṣuvikāreṣu' is printed as one token (teṣu vikāreṣu).

hindi: क्योंकि धीरे-धीरे निर्मल मणि पर भी कीचड़ अवश्य जम जाता है, इसलिए यथासमय मलों के शोधन के लिए उद्यत होना चाहिए।
english: Since, in due course, mud necessarily forms even on a spotless gem, one should rouse oneself at the proper time towards the cleansing of the impurities (mala).

text_flags.why: possible: "śodhanaṃ prati" expected (accusative before prati); final anusvāra seems lost; metre is 16 either way

notes: 'kramāt' could also be 'by sequence'. 'apaṃka' (a-paṅka) taken as 'without mud'. 'uttiṣṭheta' is literally 'should stand up', i.e. be ready to act.

hindi: संचय की चरम सीमा पर पहुँचकर वे उपेक्षित होने पर प्रायः बहुत देर बाद भी औषध के विरोधी रोगों को उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: Having reached the limit (kāṣṭhā) of accumulation, they, when neglected, produce, mostly even after a very long time, diseases that are hostile to remedies.
notes: 'te' (the accumulated doṣas) is carried over from an earlier unit; it is not named here. 'bheṣajadveṣiṇaḥ' is literally 'remedy-hating'.

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, m. acc. pl. (same form as nom.; "those whose ojas is carried off"; the ending is unclear, see notes)
f. acc. pl. (same form as nom.; object of kurvate, unit 28)

hindi: अत्यधिक स्थूलता, अग्नि का मन्द पड़ना, कुष्ठ, मेह, ओज का नष्ट होना; स्रोतों का अवरोध, अक्ष का विभ्रंश, श्वास, शोथ और पाण्डुता।
english: Excessive stoutness, decline of the digestive fire (agni), kuṣṭha, meha, loss of ojas; obstruction of the channels (srotas), impairment of the akṣa (senses), śvāsa (literally 'breath'), swelling (śvayathu) and paleness (pāṇḍutā).

text_flags.why: possible: "raudha" is not a word here; "srotorodha" (obstruction of channels) expected; the book split also reads rodha

notes: A list of conditions continuing from unit 28; the verb is not in this unit. 'hṛtaujasaḥ' is read as hṛta-ojas 'ojas carried off'; the ending -aḥ is unclear (could be a dvandva member in the plural). 'akṣa' normally means sense organ (also eye/axle); the book split reads 'akṣi' (eye), which would make it 'impairment of sight'. Disorder names (kuṣṭha, meha) are kept untranslated.

words.gloss: jaṭhara (belly; here a name in the list)

hindi: आमोह, स्तम्भ, जठर, उच्छ्राय, अलसक और दण्डक; तृप्ति, प्रमीलक, आलस्य, ग्रहणी, अर्श और भगन्दर।
english: Bewilderment (āmoha), stiffness, jaṭhara, swelling (ucchrāya), alasaka and daṇḍaka; satiety, pramīlaka, laziness, grahaṇī, arśas and bhagaṃdara.
notes: Accusative plural list continuing the objects of 'kurvate' (unit 28). 'jaṭharocchrāya' may be one item ('swelling of the belly') or two; here two. Technical disorder names are kept as names, with no modern equivalent.

words.gram: n. acc. sg. (nom. form identical; svapna-darśanam)

hindi: प्लीह, विद्रधि, विसर्प, मद, संन्यास और पीनस; छर्दि, गण्ड, कृमि, ग्रन्थि, तन्द्रा और स्वप्नदर्शन।
english: Plīha, vidradhi, visarpa, mada, saṃnyāsa and pīnasa; vomiting, gaṇḍa, worms, lumps (granthi), drowsiness (tandrālu, 'prone to drowsiness', printed with a nominative ending), and the seeing of dreams.

text_flags.why: possible: "krami" for krimi (worm); "grathi" for graṃthi (anusvāra lost, metre unchanged); and "tandrāluḥ" has a visarga inside what reads as a list, perhaps "tandrālu"

notes: In the first token, 'graṃthi + taṃdrā-' is read for printed 'grathitaṃdrā-'; the book split reads 'grathita' (knotted) instead, which would give 'knotted drowsiness', less likely. 'tandrāluḥ' (nominative, 'prone to drowsiness') does not fit the accusative list; rendered as 'drowsiness'. Line 2 does not clearly end the list; the second token joins svapna with darśanaṃ ('seeing of dreams'). Disorder names are kept untranslated.

words.gloss: of intellect and ? (reading uncertain: indriya 'sense' or nidrā 'sleep'; see flag)

hindi: कण्ठ के रोग, शिर की पीड़ा, तथा बुद्धि और — पाठ अस्पष्ट: इन्द्रिय अथवा निद्रा — का नाश; और बृंहण उपायों से तृप्त होते हुए भी तेज, वर्ण और बल का नाश।
english: Throat diseases, head-pain, and loss of intellect and (?) (printed buddhiniṃdrayoḥ; reading uncertain: 'senses' or 'sleep'); and loss of lustre (tejas), complexion and strength, even in one who is being satiated with nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) means.

text_flags.why: possible: printed "niṃdrayoḥ" is not a valid form after buddhi; the minimal edit is buddhinidrayoḥ (intellect and sleep; one anusvāra deleted); buddhīṃdriyayoḥ is the other candidate; metre (8) fits either

notes: The reading of 'buddhiniṃdrayoḥ' is uncertain; 'buddhi-nidrayoḥ' (of intellect and sleep) is a possible alternative and needs only deletion of the anusvāra. 'praṇāśaṃ' also governs the genitives of line 2. The listing continues from units 28-31. GROUPING: possibly 32 L2 (tejovarṇabalānāṃ ... bṛṃhaṇair api) pairs with 33 L1 (ucitair api cāhārair ...); see unit 34 note.

uncertain.note: [src/split] `बुद्धिनिंद्रयोः` / split `इन्द्रियोः` not a valid form — suggested: `बुद्धीन्द्रियाणां` or `बुद्धीन्द्रिययोः`

hindi: और उचित आहारों से भी, क्योंकि इसके वे नहीं बढ़ते; दोषों से लिप्त मुखों वाली, रस को वहन करने वाली शिराएँ, रस को…
english: Since even with suitable foods they do not increase in him; the vessels that carry rasa, their mouths smeared with doṣas, the rasa ...
notes: Neither line states its subject or main verb in this unit: 'vardhanti' needs a subject from the preceding unit (probably the lustre, complexion and strength just listed), and line 2 has no verb for 'rasaṃ' (the book supplies a negated verb; the Sanskrit here does not). The translation therefore stops where the text stops. 'doṣopalipta-vadanāḥ' is feminine plural to agree with śirāḥ; the printed 'vadanā' is the visarga-dropped form. See the GROUPING note on unit 34.

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] Subject "धातुएँ"/"these qualities" is not in the Sanskrit line (likely carried from neighbouring verse); verse lacks object — suggested: keep, or "तेज, वर्ण, बल"
[hindi/eng] Hindi says channels do not take up rasa (न); Sanskrit line has no negation/verb (verse continues elsewhere); Eng left as dependent fragment — suggested: Hindi/Eng join with 1.5._64_

hindi: इसलिए स्वस्थ व्यक्ति के लिए भी विधि के अनुसार वमन आदि का प्रयोग करना चाहिए; लङ्घन और पाचन से जीते गए दोष कभी-कभी प्रकुपित हो जाते हैं।
english: Therefore one should employ emesis and the like, according to rule, even for a healthy person. Doṣas conquered by fasting (laṅghana) and digestive (pācana) measures sometimes become provoked.
notes: 'vamanādīn' is not securely the printed reading: the study text records it as reconstructed from the Hindi/English ('emesis etc.') and the original may differ. It gives good sense (vamana-ādīn). 'eva' is rendered 'even' (also 'only'). GROUPING: the sense appears to run from the second line of this unit into the first line of the next, so the natural verses look offset by one line from here to unit 43 (possible regrouping: 34 L2 + 35 L1 form one couplet: 'doṣāḥ kadācit kupyanti ... / ye tu saṃśodhanaiḥ śuddhā ...'; and 33 L2 + 34 L1 would then pair. Same pattern: 35 L2 + 36 L1, 36 L2 + 37 L1, 37 L2 + 38 L1, 38 L2 + 39 L1, 39 L2 + 40 L1, 40 L2 + 41 L1, 41 L2 + 42 L1, 42 L2 + 43 L1; units 44-47 are complete verses.)

uncertain.note: [src/split] Fixed to `वमनादीन्ततो` on strength of Hindi/Eng "emesis etc."; original may differ (e.g. `वमनाद्यान्`) — suggested: `वमनादीन्ततो युंज्यात्`

hindi: परन्तु जो संशोधनों से शुद्ध हो गए हैं, उनका पुनः उत्पन्न होना नहीं होता; इसके बाद क्रम के अनुसार और योग्यता के अनुसार प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: But for those who have been purified by purifying measures (saṃśodhana) there is no re-arising; thereafter, in due order and as suitable, one should apply ...
notes: 'ye' is not explicitly the doṣas (the book's Hindi supplies 'doṣas'); the text only says 'those who/which'. The object of 'prayojayet' is in the next unit (rasāyanas, vṛṣya formulations). 'ataūrdhvaṃ' is read ataḥ ūrdhvam 'thereafter'. See GROUPING note on unit 34.
lines_deva: ये तु संशोधनैः शुद्धा न तेषां पुनरुद्भवः ॥
lines_iast: ye tu saṃśodhanaiḥ śuddhā na teṣāṃ punarudbhavaḥ ||

hindi: समय को जानने वाला सिद्ध रसायनों और वृष्य योगों का प्रयोग करे; और औषधों से क्षीण हुए व्यक्ति में पथ्य आहारों द्वारा क्रम से बृंहण करे।
english: The one who knows time (kāla) (should apply) proven rasāyana preparations and vṛṣya formulations; and, for one depleted by medicines, the wholesome nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) regimen by means of foods, step by step.
notes: The verb 'prayojayet' comes from unit 35. 'siddha' may be 'proven' or 'well prepared'. 'bheṣajakṣapite' is a locative absolute-like phrase 'when one is depleted by medicines'. 'bṛṃhaṇam' is taken as a noun with 'pathyam' as its adjective. See GROUPING note on unit 34.

words.gloss: with śāli, ṣaṣṭika, wheat, mung, meat, ghee, etc.
by combination with agreeable, kindling medicinal substances

hindi: शालि, षष्टिक, गेहूँ, मूँग, मांस, घृत आदि से, मन को प्रिय और दीपन औषधीय द्रव्यों के संयोग से, रुचि और पाचन देने वाले उपायों द्वारा।
english: With śāli rice, ṣaṣṭika rice, wheat, mung, meat, ghee and the like, through combination with agreeable, kindling (dīpana) medicinal substances, by (those) that give relish and digestion.
notes: Instrumental phrases continuing from unit 36 (āhāraiḥ). 'ruci-pakti-daiḥ' is taken as an adjective of the foods/means; 'dīpana' is 'kindling' (of agni). Food and grain names are kept as names (śāli, ṣaṣṭika are kinds of rice). 'hṛdya' is 'agreeable' (literally 'of the heart'). See GROUPING note on unit 34.

words.gloss: with oil massage, rubbing, bathing, and nirūha and sneha enemas

hindi: अभ्यङ्ग सहित उद्वर्तन, स्नान तथा निरूह और स्नेह बस्तियों से; इस प्रकार वह सुख और सब अग्नियों की तीक्ष्णता प्राप्त करता है।
english: By means of oil massage (abhyaṅga) together with rubbing (udvartana), bathing, and nirūha and sneha enemas (basti); thus he obtains comfort and keenness of all the fires.
notes: 'sābhyaṅga' is sa-abhyaṅga 'together with massage' and may attach to the whole list. 'nirūha-sneha-bastibhiḥ' is read as 'nirūha and sneha bastis' (two kinds of enema). 'pāvaka' is literally 'fire'; the book glosses it as digestive fires. See GROUPING note on unit 34.

words.gloss: clarity of intellect, complexion and senses
words.gram: dvandva then tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg.

words.gloss: arising from bhūtas, poison, wind, fire, wounds, fractures, etc.

hindi: बुद्धि, वर्ण और इन्द्रियों की निर्मलता, वृषता और आयु की दीर्घता; जो भूत, विष, वायु, अग्नि, क्षत, भङ्ग आदि से उत्पन्न होते हैं ...
english: Clarity of intellect, complexion and senses, virility, and length of life; those (disorders) that arise from bhūtas (spirits or beings), poison, wind, fire, wounds, fractures and the like ...
notes: Line 1 completes the object of 'labhate' (unit 38); line 2 begins a relative clause completed in unit 40 ('te syur āgantavo gadāḥ'). The noun 'gadāḥ' is supplied from unit 40. 'bhūta' means beings or spirits; 'vāyu' here is wind. See GROUPING note on unit 34 (39 L1 pairs with 38 L2; 39 L2 with 40 L1).

words.gloss: desire, anger, fear and the like

hindi: तथा काम, क्रोध, भय आदि से उत्पन्न होने वाले, वे आगन्तुक रोग होते हैं। प्रज्ञापराधों का त्याग, इन्द्रियों का उपशम, स्मृति।
english: And those (arising) from desire, anger, fear and the like - they would be the adventitious (āgantu) diseases. Abandonment of errors of the intellect (prajñāparādha), calming of the senses, memory.
notes: 'kāmakrodhabhayādyāḥ' is read as 'having desire, anger, fear etc. as the beginning' and taken with the relative clause of unit 39 ('those that arise from ... and those from desire ...'). The printed 'tesyur' is te syuḥ. Line 2 begins a new list of items with no verb in this unit. 'smṛti' may also be mindfulness. See GROUPING note on unit 34 (40 L1 pairs with 39 L2; 40 L2 with 41 L1).

words.gloss: knowledge of place, time and self
words.gram: dvandva then tat-puruṣa, n. nom. sg.

hindi: देश, काल और आत्मा का ज्ञान, सद्वृत्त का अनुसरण; अथर्व में विहित शान्ति कर्म, प्रतिकूल ग्रहों की अर्चना।
english: Knowledge of place, time and self; following good conduct; the pacificatory rite prescribed in the Atharva (Veda); worship of unfavourable grahas (planets or seizers).

text_flags.why: possible: "sadvṛtta" (good conduct) expected; the d of sad- appears lost; metre is unchanged

notes: 'ātma-vijñāna' may also be 'knowledge of the self (ātman)'. 'graha' is left as 'graha' (planet or seizing spirit). The items are a list with no verb in this unit. See GROUPING note on unit 34 (41 L1 pairs with 40 L2; 41 L2 with 42 L1).

words.gloss: means of not being touched by bhūtas etc.

hindi: भूत आदि के स्पर्श से बचने का उपाय अलग-अलग बताया गया है; उत्पन्न न होने के लिए संक्षेप में यह विधि दिखाई गई है।
english: The means of not being touched by bhūtas and the like has been indicated, each separately. For non-arising, this procedure has been shown in brief.
notes: 'anutpattyai' has its object in unit 43 ('nijāgantuvikārāṇām': of innate and adventitious disorders). See GROUPING note on unit 34 (42 L1 pairs with 41 L2; 42 L2 with 43).

words.gram: dvandva then tat-puruṣa, m. gen. pl.

hindi: सहज और आगन्तुक विकारों के, तथा उत्पन्न हुओं की शान्ति के लिए।
english: (For the non-arising) of innate and adventitious disorders, and for the pacification of those that have arisen.
notes: A single half-verse line; it completes unit 42 ('anutpattyai ... vidhir eṣaḥ pradarśitaḥ'): 'nija-āgantu-vikārāṇām' goes with anutpattyai and utpannānām with śāntaye. GROUPING: 42 L2 + 43 form one verse. 'nija' is 'innate'.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa (adjective), m. acc. sg., agreeing with doṣa-cayam
pres. part. vi-√śudh caus., m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: at the passing of the clouds

hindi: जो वसन्त में शीत से उत्पन्न दोषसंचय का, वर्षा के समय ग्रीष्म से उत्पन्न का, और मेघों के चले जाने पर वर्षा ऋतु के संचय का शीघ्र और भली-भाँति शोधन करता है, वह ऋतुओं से उत्पन्न रोगों को कभी प्राप्त नहीं होता।
english: One who purifies the accumulation of doṣa born of winter in spring, that born of summer in the time of clouds (the rains), and, at the passing of the clouds, that of the rainy season, quickly and properly, never incurs seasonal diseases.

text_flags.why: the scan read 'akāle'; 'abhra-' is an upstream emendation (the metre fits 22 only with it); the English '(the rains)' rests on it

notes: Upajāti, 22 syllables a line. 'abhrakāle' (the book editors replaced an original 'akāle') is metrically right (22) and gives the rainy season for the summer accumulation. 'ghanātyaye' (end of the clouds) is taken as the time after the rains (autumn in the usual reading, not stated here). The subject 'one' is supplied from 'viśodhayan'; 'doṣacayam' is understood with 'grīṣmajam' and 'vārṣikam'.
lines_deva: घनात्यये वार्षिकमाशु सम्यक् प्राप्नोति रोगानृतुजान्न जातु ॥
lines_iast: ghanātyaye vārṣikamāśu samyak prāpnoti rogānṛtujānna jātu ||

uncertain.note: [src] `अकाले` changed to `अभ्रकाले` (rainy season) on doctrine (summer Vata purified in rains) — suggested: `ग्रीष्मजमभ्रकाले`

hindi: जो नित्य हितकर आहार और विहार का सेवन करता है, विचारकर कार्य करता है, विषयों में अनासक्त है, दाता, सम, सत्यपरायण, क्षमावान् और आप्त जनों की सेवा करने वाला है, वह नीरोग होता है।
english: One who constantly follows wholesome food and conduct (āhāra and vihāra), acts after consideration, is unattached to sense-objects, is generous, even-minded, devoted to truth, forbearing, and attends upon trustworthy persons (āpta), becomes free from disease.
notes: Upajāti, 22 syllables a line. 'dātāsamaḥ' is read 'dātā samaḥ'; 'dātā asamaḥ' ('unequalled giver') is grammatically possible but gives a less natural list. 'vihāra' is general conduct or regimen; 'āpta' is a reliable, authoritative person.

words.gloss: one who has conquered the senses

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. nom. sg., agreeing with daivam

hindi: जो न पाने योग्य विषयों में प्रयत्न नहीं करता और उपाय वाले विषयों में सदा आदर रखता है, उस जितेन्द्रिय को रोग पीड़ित नहीं करते, यदि उस समय से जुड़ा दैव न हो।
english: Diseases do not afflict one who makes no effort in unobtainable matters, who always shows regard for those that have means (upāya), and who has conquered his senses, if there is no fate (daiva) joined with that time.

text_flags.why: possible: neuter nominative "daivam" expected with asti; final anusvāra lost; metre unchanged (22)

notes: Upajāti, 22 syllables a line. 'tatkālayuktaṃ ... daivaṃ' is ambiguous: 'fate that is joined with that time' (i.e. fate ripening then) is the reading used; the book renders it as an unfavourable destiny. 'anutapanti' is literally 'burn after, afflict'. 'upāyavatsu' is 'in matters that have means (to attain them)'.
lines_deva: जितेंद्रियं नोनुतपंति रोगास्तत्कालयुक्तं यदि नास्ति दैव ॥
lines_iast: jiteṃdriyaṃ nonutapaṃti rogāstatkālayuktaṃ yadi nāsti daiva ||

hindi: अनुकूल काल, मन को भाने वाले विषय, धर्मयुक्त क्रियाएँ और सुख के परिणाम वाला कर्म; वश में रहने वाला सत्त्व और निर्मल बुद्धि धीर पुरुष के लिए सदा सुख के लिए होते हैं।
english: A favourable time, agreeable sense-objects, righteous acts, and action followed by happiness; a controllable mind (sattva) and a clear intellect - these are always for the happiness of the steadfast person.
notes: Upajāti, 22 syllables a line. 'viṣayā' and 'manojñā' are visarga-dropped forms (viṣayāḥ, manojñāḥ). 'kriyāḥ karma' may be read as two items or as one phrase ('acts, action'); here two. 'sattva' is taken as 'mind' (its sense in this kind of list); it can also be 'strength of mind'.
lines_deva: कालोऽनुकूलो विषया मनोज्ञा धर्म्म्याः क्रियाःकर्म सुखानुबंधि ॥
सत्त्वं विधेयं विशदा च बुद्धिर्भवंति धीरस्य सदासुखाय ॥
lines_iast: kālo'nukūlo viṣayā manojñā dharmmyāḥ kriyāḥkarma sukhānubaṃdhi ||
sattvaṃ vidheyaṃ viśadā ca buddhirbhavaṃti dhīrasya sadāsukhāya ||

hindi: इस प्रकार रोगानुत्पादनीय नामक पाँचवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus the fifth chapter, named Rogānutpādanīya (on the non-arising of diseases). 5.
notes: Prose colophon. The first word of the title is 'roga-anutpādanīya' (literally 'diseases-not-to-be-produced', a negated gerundive of the causative; the title means the chapter on not letting diseases arise). The numeral 5 is the chapter number.
